title: The root of learning
hookLine: most Hebrew words grow from a root of three letters
carry: talmud, student, teacher: one root, learning

cards: A student, a teacher, the Talmud, and an hour of study. Four things that seem to have nothing in common. One sits at a desk.
One stands at the front. One fills a long shelf of heavy volumes. One is the time you set aside to open a book.
Say them in Hebrew and listen: talmid, melamed, Talmud, limud. The same three sounds keep surfacing, l, m, d, like one family face in a row of old photographs.
That's how Hebrew is built: three letters underneath, and a whole family of words growing out of them.

teach.b: Shoresh: a root. Four ways in. First, the idea.
A great many Hebrew words grow from a root of three consonants carrying a core meaning. Vowels, and letters added before, after or between, turn it into a noun, a verb, a person, a place.
Second, a root you've already met. Lamed, mem, dalet carries learning. Lamad: he learned.
Talmid: a student, one who learns.

Melamed: a teacher, one who makes others learn. Talmud: the great body of study. In Deuteronomy, Moses tells the people to hear the laws "that ye may learn them," and the Hebrew for learn is built on those same letters.
Third, a second root. Kaf, tav, vet carries writing.
Katav: he wrote. Michtav: a letter you'd mail. Ktav: handwriting.
And Ketuvim, the Writings, the third part of the Hebrew Bible: the Psalms, Proverbs and Ruth. Fourth, the picture in the word itself. Shoresh is the root of a tree.

teach.h: A TREE'S ROOTS BY THE WATER.
teach.b: In Jeremiah, the one who trusts in God is like a tree planted by water, sending its roots out toward the stream.

teach.h: TALMUD, STUDENT, TEACHER: ONE ROOT, LEARNING.
teach.b: You see branches, leaves and fruit; the root stays underground, holding it all together. For the next stretch of the path, we'll dig up one root a day and watch what grows out of it.

how: Students of Hebrew learn to find the three-letter root of a word, and dictionaries of biblical Hebrew are often arranged by root rather than by spelling.

games.q: a friend says the Talmud is just an old rule book. what does its own name say it is?
o: learning: it grows from lamed, mem, dalet, like student and teacher.
writing: it grows from kaf, tav, vet, like a letter.
law: it's a Greek word for a code of rules.
games.why: Talmud, talmid, melamed: the body of study, the student, the teacher, all from the root of learning.

practice: Say these slowly and listen for the three sounds that stay: lamad, talmid, melamed, Talmud, l, m, d; then katav, michtav, Ketuvim, k, t, v.
Let the words fall away and keep only the three letters, the way a root stays in the ground while the leaves come and go. If you pray, you can do the same with a word from a prayer you know.

wordCard.voice: Shoresh. A root: the three letters underneath a family of Hebrew words, and the root of a tree. Today's word.
